# 10 ways to use ChatGPT to level up your small business

Futurpreneur | July 16, 2024

As a small business owner, your marketing, communications, business and product development departments probably consist of … just you.

Even if you have a co-founder or administrative assistant to help out with the various tasks that keep your doors open and customers coming in, you’ve likely got enough tasks to keep twice as many people plenty busy. 

Enter the robots! Artificial intelligence, or AI, has reached the mainstream, and a wide variety of AI tools can help you perform a range of tasks that might otherwise cost you valuable time that could be put to better use elsewhere.

## What is ChatGPT and what can it do for you?

[ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com/) is a large language model (LLM) program that understands and generates human-like text. One of the most popular AI tools, ChatGPT, like all LLMs, has been “trained” on a massive amount of text from various sources to learn grammar, context, and information on nearly every topic on the internet. The instructions you give ChatGPT are called a prompt, and how you write the prompt influences the quality and relevance of what the bot responds with. 

It’s important to understand that while LLMs can make your business life so much easier in so many ways, they aren’t infallible, and they may not always make sense for every use case (see our Tips section for more about this!) 

Any time you put AI to work for your business, it’s important to proceed with caution and carefully weigh each situation to determine whether using it is appropriate. Additionally, since all chatbots can produce inaccurate or misleading information — and will sometimes create fictional data to provide an example or fill word count — only use what they generate as a starting point rather than a finished product. Thoroughly fact-check it — and put your own spin on it so that it sounds authentic, not robotic.

ChatGPT is free and easy to use, once you get the hang of it — and once you do, it becomes your very own virtual assistant that can understand what you’re asking it to do and respond accordingly as if engaging in a conversation. Here are 10 tasks ChatGPT can perform for you so you can maximize your time and put your focus where it’s most needed.

## 1\. Write your blog

Creating engaging content is a cornerstone of effective marketing, and a blog is a great way to speak directly to your audience to engage them and help them solve a problem. ChatGPT can write an entire blog post in less time than it takes you to tell it what to write. 

Decide on the topic of your blog post, and craft a clear prompt that tells ChatGPT what the topic is and how long it should be. Clearly communicate the main points you want to cover, outline the structure of the blog post, and provide information like the audience, keywords to include, the tone of voice (casual, formal, persuasive), and any additional information you want the bot to include. You can also keep it simple by starting with a general overview and then refining the blog from there with more and more detailed prompts.

Review your blog article for accuracy, clarity, and your brand voice before you post it on your website. Add your own insights, expertise, or personal touch to the blog post. This adds authenticity and value that AI-generated content might lack.

## 2\. Create employee manuals

Whether you own a bakery, boutique, or barber shop, if you have employees, you need an employee manual — and ChatGPT can write it for you. 

In your prompt, tell ChatGPT the structure of the employee manual—list the titles of the sections and the key information you want to include. Give an overview of your company’s purpose and mission. Ask the bot to write an introduction and table of contents.

After ChatGPT generates content for a section, review and edit it to ensure accuracy, clarity, and consistency with your company’s voice and style. You can continue to refine the content by refining your prompts. 

## 3\. Automate social media campaigns

Maintaining a consistent and engaging social media presence is a time consuming and often challenging task for many small business owners. ChatGPT can write and schedule posts, generate content ideas, respond to comments, and even assess the effectiveness of your [social media campaigns](https://www.futurpreneur.ca/en/2016/beginners-guide-to-building-a-social-media-strategy/). 

ChatGPT’s maker, OpenAI, provides API access that allows you to integrate ChatGPT into your social media platform. But before you can use it for social media posts and responses, you need to train it, which involves providing examples of the types of questions and responses you expect from users on social media and the voice and tone of your brand. Identify the triggers that will prompt the chatbot to respond, such as keywords, specific hashtags, or mentions. When the chatbot detects these triggers in incoming social media interactions, it will respond accordingly, based on how you’ve trained it.

## 4\. Generate reports

Using ChatGPT to generate reports requires giving clear instructions and data to the bot and guiding it through the process of creating the report. 

Before instructing ChatGPT, clearly outline the purpose and scope of the report. Identify the key objectives and the target audience, and create an outline for the report — break down the content into sections, headings, and subheadings. 

Collect all the relevant data, information, and sources that you’ll need to include in the report. This could be data from spreadsheets, databases, research findings, or any other relevant sources.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/61473dd4e23e175afa48c7a6/2783d7e6-a16e-49c4-a401-af94de05ddde/ChatGPT+for+small+business+marketing.jpg)

As a small business owner myself, I know how overwhelming it can be to try and keep up with marketing while running your business. That’s where ChatGPT for small business marketing comes in!

Luckily, with ChatGPT, you can automate many of your repetitive marketing tasks, it’s like having a keen and intelligent assistant available 24/7.

Of course, ChatGPT can’t run your business for you. It can make mistakes, and it _definitely_ needs your human expertise and specific instructions to work effectively. But it _can_ help you get a head start on that blog post you’ve been putting off (we all know starting is often the hardest part!) or help you re-purpose an Instagram post into a LinkedIn post in seconds.

The main benefit of ChatGPT for small business marketing is saving you time! Yes, you’ll still need to verify and edit the content ChatGPT produces, but with its help, you can get a lot more done in a short space of time, freeing you up to focus on growing your business.

In this blog post, we’ll explore **5 ways you can use ChatGPT to automate marketing**, including content creation, social media marketing, email marketing, SEO, and data analysis.

UPDATE: You can also now work WITH ChatGPT using [ChatGPT Work Mode](https://louise-laurie.co.uk/blog/i-tested-chatgpt-work-mode-for-my-small-business-heres-what-happened) - so ChatGPT can work with you on tasks such as content creation, competitor research, repetitive admin, creating reports and presentations and more.

Writing content can be one of the most time-consuming parts of marketing—whether it’s a blog post, an email, or even just a social media caption. But this is where ChatGPT comes in to make your life easier.

ChatGPT can’t write your content _exactly_ how you would (it’s not _that_ smart... yet!), but it can give you **a strong starting point**. Think of it like a brainstorming partner—it helps you get past the blank page so you can focus on refining and personalising the content.

#### **How ChatGPT can help with content creation & copywriting:**

1.  **Blog post outlines & drafts** – Need to write a blog post but don’t know where to start? ChatGPT can generate an outline or even a full first draft in seconds. You can then tweak it to match your voice and add your expertise. Alternatively, you can write a draft outline yourself and ask ChatGPT to refine it for you. I recommend this approach as it keeps the blog in your unique style and tone while still saving time.
    
2.  **Social media captions** – Struggling to come up with fresh Instagram or LinkedIn copy? Give ChatGPT a topic, and it’ll generate multiple caption ideas to choose from. Alternatively, you can ask ChatGPT to rewrite a caption in a different tone, adjust it for another platform, or tailor it to a specific audience.
    
3.  **Website copy** – Whether it’s product descriptions, an “About” page, or a sales landing page, ChatGPT can provide a structure and persuasive wording to work from. You can even give it an example of your brands ‘voice’ so that it produces copy that sounds like your brand.
    
4.  **Repurposing content** – If you’ve already written a long blog post or article, ChatGPT can help to break it down into bite-sized social media posts, emails, or even a LinkedIn article—saving you hours of effort. This is one of the main ways I use ChatGPT! For example, ChatGPT could help me to repurpose this blog post into an Instagram carousel and caption, or even a video script for YouTube.
    
5.  **Video scripts** - Speaking of video scripts…ChatGPT is a lifesaver for writing scripts. ChatGPT has honestly saved me so much time when creating my [Skillshare courses](https://www.skillshare.com/en/r/user/louise-laurie-marketing). I usually draft an outline of each lesson with key points, and then ChatGPT helps organise it into a structured script—cutting down hours of work.
    
6.  **Ad copy**\- ChatGPT can help to produce persuasive copy for all kinds of ads in seconds - whether it’s for social media ads, online banner ads, or offline ads such as leaflets.

# Why Small Business Owners Should Use AI, Such as ChatGPT (written by ChatGPT)

_**EDITOR’S NOTE: Based on our latest survey, LGBA Members wanted to know more about saving time and marketing tips. I figured this was a perfect time to start talking about AI. And, who better to talk about AI than ChatGPT itself. Created by ChatGPT with a few prompts, may I present ChatGPT!**_

_By ChatGPT_

Running a small business often means wearing multiple hats—marketing strategist, customer service representative, content creator, and more. With limited time and resources, small business owners must find innovative ways to streamline operations and maximize efficiency. This is where artificial intelligence (AI), like ChatGPT, comes in.

AI-powered tools are no longer just for big corporations with deep pockets. Small businesses can leverage AI to enhance productivity, improve customer engagement, and even drive revenue. Here’s why every small business owner should consider incorporating AI into their daily operations—and a few tools beyond ChatGPT that can help.

## **1\. Save Time on Repetitive Tasks**

Time is one of the most valuable resources for small business owners. AI can automate repetitive tasks, such as answering frequently asked customer inquiries, generating email responses, or drafting social media captions. Instead of spending hours on these activities, business owners can focus on strategy and growth.

## **2\. Enhance Customer Service**

Small businesses may not have the capacity to offer 24/7 customer support, but AI-powered chatbots can bridge the gap. Tools like ChatGPT or AI-driven customer service platforms can provide instant responses to common customer questions, improving satisfaction and engagement while freeing up staff for more complex inquiries.

## **3\. Generate Marketing Content**

Content creation can be time-consuming, whether it’s writing blog posts, product descriptions, or social media updates. AI tools can assist in brainstorming ideas, drafting content, and even optimizing it for search engines. With ChatGPT, small business owners can maintain a consistent online presence without hiring a full-time content writer.

## **4\. Improve Decision-Making with Data Insights**

AI tools can analyze customer behavior, market trends, and sales patterns, offering valuable insights that help business owners make informed decisions. Whether it’s optimizing pricing strategies or understanding what content resonates most with customers, AI-driven analytics can provide a competitive edge.

## **5\. Boost Efficiency in Operations**

From drafting contracts and proposals to organizing schedules, AI can assist with administrative tasks that typically consume hours of a business owner’s day. By integrating AI tools with project management software, email platforms, and CRMs, businesses can streamline their workflows and operate more efficiently.

## **6\. Keep Up with the Competition**

Larger businesses are already using AI to personalize marketing campaigns, automate sales processes, and enhance customer experiences. Small businesses that embrace AI can remain competitive by leveraging similar tools to improve efficiency and customer engagement.

## **7\. Affordable and Accessible Technology**

AI solutions like ChatGPT are cost-effective compared to hiring additional staff. With flexible pricing plans and free versions available, small businesses can test AI capabilities without making a significant investment. As AI technology continues to evolve, it becomes even more accessible for businesses of all sizes.

* * *

## **Five AI Tools Entrepreneurs Should Explore Beyond ChatGPT**

While ChatGPT is a powerful tool, small business owners can benefit from a variety of AI-powered platforms. Here are five AI tools to consider:

### **1\. Jasper (AI Writing Assistant)**

If you need to generate blog posts, product descriptions, or ad copy quickly, **Jasper** is an AI writing assistant designed to create high-quality content. It helps streamline content marketing efforts and ensures consistency in brand messaging.

### **2\. Grammarly (AI-Powered Writing & Editing)**

Whether you’re sending emails, writing proposals, or creating social media content, **Grammarly** ensures your writing is clear, professional, and error-free. The AI-powered tool suggests improvements in tone, grammar, and conciseness, making communication more effective.

### **3\. Canva (AI Design & Branding)**

For businesses without a dedicated graphic designer, **Canva** provides AI-powered design tools that help create marketing materials, social media graphics, presentations, and more. The platform offers templates, brand kits, and even AI-generated design suggestions.

### **4\. Pictory (AI Video Creation)**

Video marketing is essential for engaging audiences, and **Pictory** makes it easy for small business owners to create high-quality videos from blog posts or text. The AI automatically generates video content with captions, voiceovers, and stock footage, perfect for social media and websites.

### **5\. HubSpot (AI-Powered CRM & Marketing Automation)**

For managing customer relationships and automating marketing tasks, **HubSpot** offers AI-powered tools that assist with lead tracking, email marketing, and sales pipeline management. It helps businesses maintain strong customer relationships with minimal manual effort.

* * *

## **Why AI Should Not Replace Professional Vendors**

While AI can be an incredibly useful tool, it should not completely replace the expertise of professional vendors. Small business owners should be mindful of when to use AI and when to rely on human professionals for more nuanced and specialized work. Here’s why:

### **1\. AI Lacks Human Creativity and Strategy**

AI-generated content and designs are based on existing data patterns, which means they lack true originality and strategic thinking. While AI tools can assist in brainstorming, professional marketers, designers, and copywriters bring creative vision and brand storytelling that AI simply cannot replicate.

### **2\. Legal, Financial, and Compliance Risks**

AI can generate contracts, financial reports, and even legal documents, but it cannot replace a professional accountant or attorney. Business owners should always consult legal and financial experts to ensure compliance with laws and regulations, as AI-generated recommendations may not be fully accurate or up to date.
